item.title: ‘Collaborating in Conflict: The Yeats Family and the Public Arts’: A Must-See for Poets and Painters Alike
item.description: This Sunday, the McMullen Museum of Art opened Collaborating in Conflict: The Yeats Family and the Public Arts, is a new, must-see exhibition on campus this semester.

item.title: UGBC To Provide All Freshmen With Free Laundry Supplies
item.description: UGBC voted to extend and expand its free laundry supply program to all first-year laundry rooms on Tuesday night, following a successful pilot program last spring.

item.title: BHM Opening Ceremony Emphasizes Resistance and Restoration in Overcoming Adversity
item.description: Boston College faculty, students, and community members came together Tuesday evening to celebrate the beginning of Black History Month and call for resistance through joy and community.

item.title: Planning and Development Board Approves Newton Centre Site Plan Review
item.description: Newton’s Planning and Development Board discussed a site plan review for the property at 20 Willow Street in Newton Centre on Monday, revealing the challenge of balancing change and community character as the city looks to expand its housing stock.

item.title: The Cinematic Experience: How Watching a Movie Is Actually Productive
item.description: I was partaking in my usual homework-evading Instagram scroll when a particular post caught my attention. It was a joke along the lines of, “My phone addiction is so bad, watching a movie feels productive.”

item.title: “Now, It’s Their Turn”: Despite Losing Some Stars, BC Lacrosse Is Ready To Dominate
item.description: Boston College lacrosse's 2025 season ended earlier than the Eagles expected it to. Down its top four offensive options from a year ago, a new-look BC comes into 2026 focused on leaving the past in the rearview mirror and reaching the college lacrosse mountaintop once again.

item.title: Timothy Cohoon Appointed Newton Police Chief, Vows To Prioritize Trust Amid ICE Concerns
item.description: Newton’s Public Safety and Transportation Committee appointed Timothy Cohoon, former chief of the Braintree Police Department, as Newton’s next police chief on Wednesday.

item.title: Syracuse Dominates the Boards, Beats BC 93–59 for Eagles’ 17th Straight Loss
item.description: Syracuse used a strong second quarter to gain 21-point halftime lead over Boston College women's basketball, and BC was not able to catch up as the Eagles suffered their 17-straight loss in a 93–59 blowout.

item.title: More Than a Game: Berry Reflects on the Lessons and Connections Gained From ‘Jeopardy!’ Tournament of Champions
item.description: Cameron Berry didn’t think he’d ever return to the screen after winning $26,600 from Jeopardy!, but the assistant director of applications and data analysis became a local star upon his reappearance on Jeopardy! Tournament of Champions (TOC).
